title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 309: The Pyrocene: Fire, Humans, and the Shaping of Earth
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 309 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Pyrocene: Fire, Humans, and the Shaping of Earth

Paragraph 1. For over one hundred years, western forest managers saw fire as a dangerous enemy. Governments tried to stop every wildfire in forests. However, historian Stephen Pyne says this idea was a big mistake. Fire is not just a destroyer; it is a natural part of healthy forests and grasslands. For thousands of years, humans have used fire to shape the land around them.

Paragraph 2. Long ago, early humans learned how to make, keep, and carry fire. This skill changed the human body over time. Cooking food made hard roots and meat soft and easy to eat. Because cooked food needed less chewing, human jaws and stomachs became smaller, while human brains grew much larger.

Paragraph 3. Native peoples in Australia, North America, and southern Africa used small fires as a smart land tool. Instead of waiting for huge wildfires, they carefully lit small, cool fires across the land. These gentle burns cleared old bushes, helped new grass grow for wild animals, and removed dry leaves. Because dry fuel never piled up, giant dangerous fires almost never happened.

Paragraph 4. Later, European settlers banned native people from setting these small fires. When workers stopped every tiny fire, huge amounts of dead wood piled up on forest floors. Today, hotter global weather turns this extra fuel into massive firestorms. These extreme fires burn so hot that they even destroy the soil and kill hidden plant seeds.

q1.text: For more than a century, western forest managers viewed fire as a threat.

steps: Đoạn 1: "For over one hundred years, western forest managers saw fire as a dangerous enemy."

q2.text: Historian Stephen Pyne worked as a firefighter in Australia for ten years.

steps: Đoạn 1: Bài chỉ nêu ông là nhà sử học (historian), không nhắc ông từng làm lính cứu hỏa ở Úc.

q3.text: Native peoples always lit huge, extremely hot fires across open lands.

steps: Đoạn 3: Họ chủ động đốt các đám cháy nhỏ và nhẹ (small, cool fires), không phải cháy khổng lồ.

q4.text: Banning small fires caused extra dead material to build up in forests.

steps: Đoạn 4: Cấm đốt nhỏ khiến gỗ khô chất đống khổng lồ trên nền rừng.
